seoTitle: Hair Salon Email & SMS Marketing Guide for Rebooking
description: Email, SMS and client retention for hair salons and barbershops: building a list, scripts, segmentation, templates and sequences that bring clients back.
intro: This guide collects our articles on email and SMS marketing for hair salons, barbershops and nail salons. It covers building a client list, text message scripts and timing, email templates and sequences, segmentation and a UK-specific guide. It is for owners who want existing clients to rebook more often without relying on social media algorithms.

If your budget is limited, begin with the list-building and SMS articles. Make sure you have permission to contact clients, collect emails and phone numbers at booking, and send one useful message a month before trying anything more complex. Many booking apps already include basic email and text tools, so check yours first.

Simple reminders, rebooking nudges and last-minute slot texts are easy to handle yourself. Segmentation, automated sequences and compliance rules take more care, particularly across different countries. If you want that set up properly, DataLatte can help, but start with what your booking software already offers.

faq.q: Is SMS or email better for hair salons?
faq.a: They do different jobs. Text messages suit short-notice items like open slots and reminders, while email suits longer updates and offers. Many salons use both, with SMS used sparingly.

faq.q: How often should a salon email or text clients?
faq.a: Less than you might think. A monthly email and occasional texts for specific openings is a reasonable start for most salons. Watch unsubscribe rates and reply behavior to adjust.

faq.q: Do I need permission to text my clients?
faq.a: Generally yes. Rules differ by country, such as TCPA in the US and PECR and GDPR in the UK, so get clear consent and offer an easy opt-out. This is general information, not legal advice, so check the rules where you operate.

faq.q: What should I write in a salon marketing email?
faq.a: Keep it short and useful: a rebooking reminder, a new service, or an opening this week with a clear booking button. Our template and sequence articles give examples to adapt. Personal tone usually works better than heavy design.
